data.text: All three scenarios look covered so far; writing the findings file now.

All three scenarios hold, so I wrote `{"findings": []}` to `openspec/changes/284-latest-task-attribution/.run/validator/findings.json`. I judged this by reading the code and tests; I ran no build or test command, as instructed.

- **Two later tasks measured the path:** The new `src/core/run/scope-attribution.ts` handles this. When more than one later task measured the path, it credits the highest-numbered one whose done marker records the current hash and adds `source: "measures"`. When none match, it records `ambiguous`. `tests/scope-credit.test.ts` covers both rows, and the `h2`/`h3` row would fail on the base code, which always recorded `ambiguous`. The no-hash row gives `ambiguous` on the base too, but that matches old behavior, so it isn't a `passes_without_change` problem.
- **Two later tasks named the path:** Paths named by `file_changed` events use the same latest-matching rule, with no `source` key. `tests/scope-latest-credit.test.ts` has all five rows. The first three would fail on the base code, and the two `ambiguous` rows match old behavior.
- **A third task extends the file again:** `src/watcher/auto-recertify.ts` now starts the chain at the first end event whose `before` equals the recorded hash, instead of requiring the first event to match. `tests/auto-recertify-repeat.test.ts` runs four watcher cycles and checks every part of the THEN: no blocked cycle, no `regressed/1.md`, the current hash, `recertification_count: 2`, and the second event's `automatic: true` with attribution `3` / `measures`. On the base code, the old chain check would halt task 1 at the fourth cycle.

The patch also carries unrelated changes merged in from main (the Rust inbox work and the PLANNER.md bullet). The scenarios don't cover them, so I didn't judge them.
